observed_order: Ultrasound Abdomen (US ABD LIMIT, SINGLE ORGAN)

aqc_summary.assumption: Persistent focal right-sided pain in pregnancy remains unresolved after a broadly normal complete ultrasound; upper-abdominal disease is less likely but a targeted source remains uncertain.
aqc_summary.question: Is there a specific targeted-organ abnormality explaining persistent right-sided pain?
aqc_summary.prior_test_interpretation: The complete ultrasound was limited relative to the focal lower-abdominal/appendiceal question.

acr_mappings.variant_text: Pregnant woman. Right lower quadrant pain, fever, leukocytosis. Suspected appendicitis. Initial imaging.

supported: mild leukocytosis and unresolved intra-abdominal concern
unknown_or_ambiguous: the AQC target is generically worded rather than explicitly appendiceal at this step
predicate_instantiation.stage_relation: observed step is next imaging after a complete US, whereas the ACR variant is initial imaging

observed_action_relation.relation: action-family correspondence; protocol and sequential role are not represented

deviation_assessment: No clear action-level deviation, but no exact ACR Context covers a targeted repeat US after an initial US incompletely addressed the relevant Q.
patient_to_acr_instantiation: Treat pregnancy and focal pain as activating the pregnant RLQ pathway despite incomplete fever criteria.
Interpret the prior negative findings question-by-question rather than calling the whole study negative.
Infer that nonassessment of the appendix/lower-abdominal target leaves the clinically consequential requirement open.

bridge_operations.description: Convert a broadly normal prior study into partial coverage because it did not assess the target required by the current Q.
Move from complete abdominal US to a focused target/protocol without treating this as a new modality choice.
Use pregnancy/radiation avoidance to sustain a non-ionizing sequence while uncertainty remains.

residuals.description: The target is called an upper-abdominal organ/region even though the trajectory concern is lower-abdominal/appendiceal; the generic exam name may have driven an unstable reconstruction.
Crohn disease and mild pelvicaliectasis complicate the source frame but are not represented in the closest ACR variant.

candidate_ai_roles: extract whether required anatomy was visualized
map supported and missing ACR predicates
ai_assessment.safety_boundary: AI can surface the incomplete target and candidate variant, but a clinician must resolve the ambiguous anatomy and decide whether repeat US is appropriate.

observed_order: Ultrasound Abdomen (LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN))

aqc_summary.assumption: CT-detected gallstones and subtle inflammatory change make gallbladder disease plausible but do not establish acute cholecystitis.
aqc_summary.question: Does targeted sonography confirm acute cholecystitis or clinically significant gallbladder pathology?
aqc_summary.prior_test_interpretation: CT was diagnostic technically but left the gallbladder-specific question indeterminate.

acr_mappings.variant_text: Right upper quadrant pain. Suspected biliary disease. Initial imaging.

predicate_instantiation.stage_relation: ACR says initial imaging; this is targeted imaging after an equivocal CT

observed_action_relation.relation: strong action-family correspondence under the initial-imaging variant

acr_mappings.variant_text: Right upper quadrant pain. Fever, elevated WBC count. Suspected biliary disease. Negative or equivocal ultrasound. Next imaging study.

contradicted_or_absent: the prior equivocal test was CT, not ultrasound
predicate_instantiation.stage_relation: next imaging aligns, but the required prior-test type does not

observed_action_relation.relation: US is not a rated next action in this variant

deviation_assessment: The observed US is strongly concordant with the initial suspected-biliary action set, but the actual CT-to-US sequence has no exact ACR variant. Calling it either concordant or deviant without separating Context and Action would be misleading.
patient_to_acr_instantiation: Map focal RUQ symptoms and leukocytosis to suspected biliary disease.
Treat the CT result as equivocal relative to acute cholecystitis despite being technically diagnostic.
Choose the initial-imaging action logic while simultaneously occupying a next-imaging trajectory stage.

bridge_operations.description: Distinguish diagnostic CT adequacy from incomplete capability for the sonographic acute-cholecystitis question.
Combine clinical predicates from an initial variant with the temporal state of a next-imaging variant because no single ACR Context fits.
Translate equivocal CT gallbladder findings into a targeted US question rather than simply choosing the highest-rated next action after equivocal US.

residuals.description: Severe cardiopulmonary disease and anticoagulation raise the evidentiary threshold for intervention but are not part of the closest ACR Contexts.

candidate_ai_roles: separate study adequacy from question coverage
show action ratings under each candidate Context
ai_assessment.safety_boundary: AI should display the stage mismatch and avoid assigning a single definitive ACR concordance label.

aqc_summary.assumption: Shock and a rigid peritonitic abdomen imply a possible intra-abdominal catastrophe despite a prior noncontrast CT without a clear source.
aqc_summary.question: Is there a surgically or interventionally treatable source missed by the earlier CT?
aqc_summary.prior_test_interpretation: The prior CT reduced confidence in gross perforation but did not explain the acute abdomen.

acr_mappings.variant_text: Left lower quadrant pain. Suspected complication(s) of diverticulitis. Initial imaging.

contradicted_or_absent: the AQC does not establish left lower quadrant localization or suspected diverticulitis
unknown_or_ambiguous: whether the disease-stratum label reflects the active pre-order frame
predicate_instantiation.stage_relation: observed step is repeat/next CT; ACR variant is initial imaging

observed_action_relation.procedure: CT abdomen and pelvis without IV contrast
observed_action_relation.relation: approximate protocol/action match, but only under a weak Context match and with abdomen-versus-abdomen/pelvis difference

deviation_assessment: The action resembles an ACR-rated option, but Context support is insufficient to call the decision guideline-concordant or deviant. This is a key action-match-without-context-match counterexample.
patient_to_acr_instantiation: Recognize severe clinical deterioration as justification to reopen source localization after a prior negative/indeterminate study.
Test whether the available LLQ/diverticulitis topic is truly active rather than inferring it from cohort membership.
Retain out-of-scope as a valid result when the record supports undifferentiated acute abdomen rather than an ACR variant.

bridge_operations.description: Clinical shock/peritonitis reopens a previously investigated source question even without a new clean guideline Context.
Interpret a negative noncontrast CT as insufficient for the active treatable-source question rather than as closure.
Refuse forced mapping when action similarity exists but the required presentation and condition predicates do not.

residuals.description: Shock, rigid abdomen, cirrhosis/ascites, and possible peritonitis create an undifferentiated emergency state not represented by the available LLQ variants.
The reason for repeating a noncontrast rather than contrast-enhanced CT is not recoverable from the AQC fields alone.

ai_assessment.safety_boundary: Emergency source-control and imaging decisions remain clinician-led; AI's useful role is mismatch detection and structured evidence display.

aqc_summary.assumption: Acute pancreatitis is established; CT and US show biliary/pancreatic duct dilation but no definite stone, leaving occult obstruction plausible.
aqc_summary.question: Is there an occult ductal obstructing lesion that could be targeted for intervention?
aqc_summary.prior_test_interpretation: Ultrasound was technically diagnostic but only partially capable because it did not identify the lesion explaining duct dilation.

acr_mappings.variant_text: Right upper quadrant pain. No fever and no high white blood cell (WBC) count. Suspected biliary disease. Negative or equivocal ultrasound. Next imaging study.

supported: equivocal ultrasound relative to the obstructing-lesion question

observed_action_relation.procedure: MRI abdomen without and with IV contrast with MRCP
observed_action_relation.relation: strong family/protocol correspondence if the recorded MRCP included contrast

acr_mappings.variant_text: Suspected acute pancreatitis. First time presentation. Epigastric pain and increased amylase and lipase. Less than 48 to 72 hours after symptom onset. Initial imaging.

contradicted_or_absent: this is not initial imaging and pancreatitis is already established

observed_action_relation.procedure: MRI abdomen without and with IV contrast with MRCP
observed_action_relation.relation: action correspondence but weaker rating under a poorly matched initial-pancreatitis Context

deviation_assessment: The order looks strongly concordant only after remapping the trajectory from an acute-pancreatitis topic to the RUQ/biliary next-imaging topic. That cross-topic remapping is itself part of the missing middle.
patient_to_acr_instantiation: Reframe the active problem from pancreatitis severity to biliary mechanism/obstruction.
Interpret duct dilation plus nonvisualized stone as an equivocal ultrasound for the lesion-specific Q.
Map the next decision to the RUQ next-imaging variant while retaining pancreatitis as the causal clinical frame.

bridge_operations.description: Move from the pancreatitis guideline topic to a biliary/RUQ Context when the unresolved downstream question concerns obstruction.
Treat ultrasound as equivocal because it shows secondary ductal signs but not the required obstructing lesion.
Advance from disease confirmation to identifying a lesion that would determine ERCP or other intervention.

residuals.description: The exact contrast protocol encoded by the local MRCP order name is ambiguous.

ai_assessment.safety_boundary: AI may recommend candidate Contexts and expose why they fit; clinician confirmation is required for protocol choice and intervention planning.
